note: Editorial findings raised during verification. Each one is either (a) a direct contradiction observed on an official page, (b) a derived count from this dataset, or (c) a policy limitation. Every finding carries a source URL. Severity: high = could cost you money; medium = needs an answer before buying; low = informational.

findings.title: Blue Nile's 18K ring page contradicts itself on the metal
findings.detail: The title and specification block of the Floral Marquise ring say '18K White Gold' / 'Metal: 18K White Gold'. The Product Details paragraph on the very same page says the ring is 'artfully crafted from warmly lustrous 14k yellow gold'. Both statements cannot be true. This is the clearest proof in the dataset that a karat claim on a product page is not verification.
findings.evidence: Title: 'Floral Marquise Diamond Engagement Ring in 18k White Gold' · Spec: 'Metal 18K White Gold' · Product Details: 'artfully crafted from warmly lustrous 14k yellow gold'
findings.action: Ask Blue Nile in writing which metal the ring is made from before ordering, and confirm the karat on the invoice.

findings.title: Only {n_weight_published_total} of {n_combined} listings publish a weight - none from this pass's five retailers
findings.detail: Within this pass, {n_weight_published} of {n_solid_gold} gold listings state the finished ring weight in grams. Across the combined dataset ({n_combined} listings, {n_sellers_total} sellers) {n_weight_published_total} publish a weight - and not one of them is a clean gold-only figure: they are variously labelled 'approximate metal weight', given as a total item weight that includes the stone, or stated as an approximate figure covering more than one metal option. Aurate's product feed does carry an undocumented numeric 'weight' field, but it repeats across variants and is never described as the finished item weight, so it was deliberately not used.
findings.evidence: This pass: {n_weight_published} of {n_solid_gold} listings state a weight. Combined: {n_weight_published_total} of {n_combined}, each qualified as approximate, inclusive of the stone, or spanning metal options.
findings.action: Ask the seller in writing for the gold-only weight in grams before paying, and keep the reply. Never substitute a total item weight (which includes the stone) for a gold weight - the difference can be a large share of the metal.

findings.title: None of this pass's five retailers states a hallmark or maker's-mark policy
findings.detail: Under 15 U.S.C. 297, a quality mark such as '14K' must be accompanied by the manufacturer's or dealer's trademark or name. None of this pass's five retailers publishes a hallmark policy on the pages checked. A parallel pass did record hallmark observations on {n_other_hallmark} of its {n_other_items} listings, which proves stamps can be documented when a seller photographs or states them - but the policy itself is still not promised in writing anywhere in this dataset.
findings.evidence: This pass: 0 of 5 retailer policy pages mention a hallmark or maker's mark. Combined: {n_other_hallmark} of {n_combined} listings state an observed hallmark.
findings.action: Before paying, ask for a close-up photograph of the inside of the band showing both the karat stamp and the maker's mark, and have the ring XRF-tested or inspected on arrival.

findings.title: {n_solid_gold_null} of {n_solid_gold} listings never use the word 'solid'
findings.detail: The checklist requires the listing itself to say solid gold. {n_solid_gold_null} of the {n_solid_gold} solid-gold listings (five Blue Nile settings and two Ring Concierge rings) state a karat but never use the word 'solid'. Seven more rely on a brand-level policy rather than the listing. Mejuri states 'solid gold' in both of its listings, and Catbird carries 'Solid' in the product name.
findings.evidence: Listings with solid_gold = null: {n_solid_gold_null}. Listings with solid_gold = true stated only at brand level: {n_solid_gold_brand}. Listings stating solid gold on the listing: {n_solid_gold_listing}.
findings.action: Get the words 'solid 14k gold' (or 18k) into the order confirmation or an email before paying.

findings.title: Ring Concierge's Trustpilot score is based on 7 reviews and an unclaimed profile
findings.detail: The 2.7 score is not statistically meaningful with 7 reviews, and Trustpilot itself notes the company has not invited customers, so the reviews 'may not be representative'. The written complaints are still worth reading: a late delivery pushing an order past the 30-day return window, and a warranty claim refused as wear and tear.
findings.evidence: '7 reviews · TrustScore 2.7 · Unclaimed profile' and 'hasn't invited their customers, so reviews may not be representative'
findings.action: Treat the score as low-confidence. Ask for the return-window start date in writing, and keep delivery records.

findings.title: Ring Concierge advertises a lifetime warranty while its refund policy says 3 years
findings.detail: The site banner and product pages say 'LIFETIME WARRANTY' / 'Complimentary Lifetime Warranty', but the Refund policy page states: 'We guarantee our pieces for 3 years from the date of purchase against manufacturer defects.' Which term governs is not stated.
findings.evidence: Banner: 'LIFETIME WARRANTY' · Refund policy: 'We guarantee our pieces for 3 years from the date of purchase against manufacturer defects.'
findings.action: Ask for the written warranty terms before purchase.

findings.title: Blue Nile excludes resized rings from returns and limits free returns to two per year
findings.detail: The 30-day money-back guarantee lists 'items resized after initial purchase' as ineligible for return or exchange, and allows only 'two complimentary returns per customer, per year'. Resizing before you inspect the ring can therefore forfeit your return right.
findings.evidence: 'items resized after initial purchase ... are not eligible for return or exchange' · 'Two complimentary returns are allowed per customer, per year.'
findings.action: Inspect and have the ring independently tested BEFORE any resizing.

findings.title: Short return windows: Aurate 15 days, Catbird 20 days (plus a $9 fee)
findings.detail: Two retailers fall well below a 30-day inspection window. Aurate allows 15 days from fulfilment for domestic orders (21 days international), and Catbird allows 20 days from delivery with a $9 return-shipping charge deducted from the refund. International Catbird sales are final.
findings.evidence: Aurate: '15-day return window starting from the day your item gets fulfilled' · Catbird: 'within 20 days of the date your package was delivered ... An $9 charge for return shipping will be deducted'
findings.action: Book the independent jeweller appointment before the ring arrives, so testing happens inside the window.

findings.title: Ring Concierge rings mix two metals - a single karat claim cannot cover the whole ring
findings.detail: The listings describe a yellow-gold band with platinum prongs. A '14k' claim describes the band, not the setting holding the stone, so a purity check of one part does not verify the other.
findings.evidence: Product image description: '2 carat Oval Diamond Engagement Ring in Yellow Gold Whisper Thin Hidden Halo band with Platinum Prongs'
findings.action: Ask which parts are gold and which are platinum, and get both tested.

findings.title: Mejuri's main /help hub requires JavaScript, while direct leaf FAQ articles render server-side
findings.detail: Mejuri's root help hub (/world/en/help) renders blank without JavaScript, hiding policy exclusions from plain-text readers unless navigated directly to server-rendered leaf FAQ subpages such as /faq/return-exchanges/what-is-the-standard-return-policy (confirming free 30-day returns in US/CA/UK/AU/DE and non-returnable exclusions for engraved/monogrammed, piercing, gift card, and 'Before We Melt' items). Live re-verification also found no voice customer phone line (+1-310-597-4745 / +1-855-496-1110 SMS & contact@mejuri.com only).
findings.evidence: 'We offer free 30-day returns & exchanges starting from the day the shipment is delivered or picked up in-store.'
findings.action: Save a PDF of the full server-rendered Mejuri return-policy leaf page and confirm exact gram weight in writing before checkout.

findings.title: In this pass, 18K prices exist only for Blue Nile settings
findings.detail: Aurate sells 18k versions of the rings in this dataset, but its collection page shows a single 'From' price that reflects the 14k option. No 18k Aurate price was captured, so none is shown. Only two 18K listings in this pass (both Blue Nile settings, centre stone excluded) have a verified price. The parallel dataset contributes further 18K rows (Tiffany, Ross-Simons, Wilson's) on its own evidence.
findings.evidence: Aurate collection page shows 'From' prices only; 18k pricing requires selecting the variant, which was not captured.
findings.action: Select the 18k variant on the product page to see the real 18k price before comparing.

findings.title: Two independent spot-price sources agree to within 0.06%
findings.detail: GoldPrice.org showed $4,022.22/oz (23 Oct 2026, 05:55 NY Time) and the World Gold Council showed $4,024.45/oz (data as of 22 Oct 2026, read 23 Oct 2026). The $2.23 gap (0.055%) is consistent with normal intraday movement and aligns with Dataset C's simultaneous Kitco ($4,022.70/oz) and BullionVault ($4,024.23/oz) quotes.
findings.evidence: GoldPrice.org $4,022.22/oz · World Gold Council $4,024.45/oz · difference $2.23 (0.055%)
findings.action: None - this is a control check, not a problem.

findings.title: Aurate's $2,858 solitaire is "Exchange for size only. Final Sale!" on a page that also shows a "Free Returns" badge
findings.detail: The live product page for the 2ct Round Lab Grown Diamond Solitaire Ring carries two notices — "Exchange for size only. Final Sale!" and "Exchange only! Return & cancellation policy." — both linking to Aurate's terms-conditions-exchange-only page. The same page displays a "Free Returns" service badge and "Lifetime Warranty", and Aurate's retailer record already notes that items marked 'exchange only' cannot be refunded. The listing-level notice is the one that governs this ring, and it removes the refund right entirely.
findings.evidence: "Exchange for size only." · "Final Sale!" · "Exchange only! Return & cancellation policy." · same page: "Free Returns" badge · price on the same page "$2,858" for "Rate - 14k GOLD", "Color - Yellow", "Size - 7", "In Stock • Ready to Ship"
findings.action: Treat this listing as non-refundable until Aurate confirms otherwise in writing. Under the buying checklist this is a walk-away candidate: no refund means no exit if the independent inspection or XRF test on arrival fails. If you still buy it, pay by credit card so the issuer's dispute route remains open, and inspect before any resizing.

findings.title: Dataset A said "no ring weight" for the Aurate solitaire — the listing does publish one, as a range
findings.detail: The record carried weight_status "not published" and a flag note reading "No ring weight in grams on the listing". The live specs block publishes "Weight: 5.5-8.5g". It is a range covering the 14k, 18k and platinum versions, so it still cannot be used as this ring's weight — weight_g stays null and no midpoint was taken — but the claim that nothing was published was wrong and has been corrected. Recording "the seller publishes nothing" when the seller publishes something is the same class of error as inventing a number: it is a statement about a source that the source does not support.
findings.evidence: Specs block on the product page: "Weight: 5.5-8.5g" (with "Width: 2.75mm", "Thickness: 1.8mm", "SKU: AU5760")
findings.action: Ask Aurate for the gram weight of the exact variant (14k yellow gold, size 7) in writing, plus whether it is gold-only or includes the stone. Until then the price-per-gram test cannot be run on this ring, and the calculator is left with no weight rather than a guessed one.

findings.title: A 3% fee belonging to Wilson's had been attached to Sarraf in the flag legend
findings.detail: Flag RET7 read: "A cancelled order is charged a 3% card-processing fee (Wilson's terms state the same fee structure)." Sarraf's return policy was re-read end to end on the live page and contains no such fee. The 3% charge is Wilson's, verbatim: "Please note that orders cancelled prior to shipment will not be refunded for credit card processing fees incurred at the rate of 3%." The fees Sarraf actually publishes are a $25.00 non-refundable engraving fee and, for warranty repair or replacement, "a Shipping and handling fee of $100.00 or 10% of purchase price which ever amount is greater". RET7 has been rewritten to Sarraf's own words and the transplant recorded here.
findings.evidence: Sarraf: "Engraving and shipping Charges are nonrefundable" · "the $25.00 engraving fee is non-refundable" · "$100.00 or 10% of purchase price which ever amount is greater" · no 3% fee anywhere in the policy. Wilson's: "credit card processing fees incurred at the rate of 3%" (stated twice, for domestic and international orders).
findings.action: None outstanding — corrected. This is logged because it is a live example of cross-seller contamination: a true fact about one seller reused as a fact about another. The hunt that found it was reading a policy page to the end instead of trusting a summary of it.

findings.title: Automic Gold's return window was recorded as unstated; the page states 30 days, and states its lead time three ways
findings.detail: Dataset B's seller record said only "Free returns stated on the product page, US only". The same page's Shipping & Returns section states "Returns can be made within 30 days of the delivery date. Free return shipping on US orders. Engraved items are final sale and cannot be returned." — so the window is now sourced. The page also gives its lead time twice with different numbers ("Production time is 4-8 business days" in the buy box; "Production time is 1-2 weeks", or "2-3 weeks" with engraving, in the policy section), which is recorded as flag SPEC2 rather than resolved by picking one.
findings.evidence: "Returns can be made within 30 days of the delivery date." · "Free return shipping on US orders." · "Engraved items are final sale and cannot be returned." · "Production time is 4-8 business days" vs "Production time is 1-2 weeks" / "2-3 weeks" with engraving
findings.action: Ask Automic to confirm the ship date in writing before ordering; note that the 30-day clock starts at delivery, and that adding engraving both lengthens the wait and makes the ring final sale.

findings.title: Ross-Simons and Catbird return policies were "Not verified" in Dataset B while Dataset A already had Catbird's quoted
findings.detail: The two datasets disagreed about the same retailer: data/retailers.json carried Catbird's 20-day window, $9 fee and final-sale list verbatim from catbirdnyc.com/returns, while data/sellers.json said "Not verified — no official return-policy page was captured" and flagged POL1. Ross-Simons had no policy page in either dataset. Both official pages were read live in this pass; both seller records now carry sourced terms, Ross-Simons' phone (800-835-0919) and email (customerservice@ross-simons.com) and Catbird's email (customerservice@catbirdnyc.com) are filled from their official contact pages, and POL1 now applies only to James Allen, whose product URLs redirect to Blue Nile.
findings.evidence: Ross-Simons: "30-Day No-Risk Return Guarantee" · "30 days from the date you receive your order" · "a flat fee of $4.95 for return shipping and handling" · "Merchandise that has been damaged, altered, or resized by a jeweler other than Ross-Simons cannot be accepted for return." Catbird: "within 20 days of the date your package was delivered" · "An $9 charge for return shipping will be deducted from your refund" · "All international sales are final."
findings.action: Closed for both sellers. The residual risk is structural: two datasets describing the same retailer can drift apart, so any future edit to a return policy should be applied to data/retailers.json and data/sellers.json together.

findings.title: Third independent read of the gold spot anchor: $4,028.53/oz live against $4,026.79 and $4,024.36 on file
findings.detail: The World Gold Council page was fetched again in this pass and read "Gold Spot price USD /oz 4,028.53" with "Data as of 21 October, 2026" and "Market Data: Provided by ICE Data Services" — the same publisher and the same market date as the stored snapshot of $4,024.36, +0.10% apart. Two earlier passes recorded the same live figure independently. The stored snapshots are dated captures and are deliberately NOT overwritten: the calculator must keep reproducing the numbers printed on the pages. The live reading is recorded here and in data/reverification-p3.json as corroboration.
findings.evidence: Live 4,028.53 USD/oz (WGC, "Data as of 21 October, 2026") vs stored 4,024.36 (WGC, same market date) and 4,026.79 (GoldPrice.org, 22 Oct 2026 07:07 NY)
findings.action: None — control check. If a future pass refreshes the anchor, it must re-run the calculator and rebuild every page so the printed melt values stay reproducible from the data.

findings.title: Sarraf's recorded e-mail address was wrong and its cited policy page returns 404
findings.detail: data/sellers.json listed Sarraf's e-mail as info@sarraf.com with contact_source https://www.sarraf.com/pages/contact-us.html. That page (which redirects to https://www.sarraf.com/contact-us/) publishes no e-mail address at all - only a contact form, two phone numbers and business hours - so the recorded address was unsupported by its own citation. Sarraf's official About page prints 'E-mail: service@sarraf.com', and the returns policy page requires wholesale return requests to go to the same address. Separately, the policy_source recorded for this seller, https://www.sarraf.com/pages/returns-and-refunds.html, returns '404 Error - Page not found' with the page title 'Sarraf - Not Found'; the live policy page is https://www.sarraf.com/30-day-returns-and-exchange-policy/, reached from Sarraf's own policy index. Both values were corrected on 2026-10-23 and the dead-link class of defect recorded as flag SRC1.
findings.evidence: About page verbatim: 'Phone: (888) 4-SARRAF ( 888-472-7723)  FAX: (213) 627-5212  E-mail: service@sarraf.com'. Returns page verbatim: 'All return require prior authorization. You must submit your request for return to service@sarraf.com'. Dead URL response verbatim: '404 Error - Page not found ... Uh oh, looks like the page you are looking for has moved or no longer exists.'
findings.action: Corrected in data/sellers.json: email service@sarraf.com, contact_source the About page, policy_source the live returns page. Any buyer contacting Sarraf should use service@sarraf.com.
findings.subject: S-SARRAF

findings.title: Automic Gold's cited return-policy URL returns 404, so its resize claim had no source
findings.detail: data/sellers.json cited https://www.automicgold.com/pages/return-policy as Automic's policy_source. Fetched on 2026-10-23 it returns '404 Not Found - Automic Gold'. The live page is https://www.automicgold.com/policies/refund-policy, and it does confirm the recorded window verbatim: 'Automic Gold offers free returns within 30 days of the delivery date for customers who reside in the U.S. You will be provided with one prepaid shipping label per order. For additional returns and exchanges, shipping fees may apply.' The resize_policy value resting on the dead URL ('Custom-altered or resized rings beyond standard stock are final sale') could not be re-sourced, because the live page's resizing clause was not captured verbatim in this pass; it has been set to null with a note rather than carried forward unsourced.
findings.evidence: Live page verbatim: 'Automic Gold offers free returns within 30 days of the delivery date for customers who reside in the U.S. You will be provided with one prepaid shipping label per order.' Free-label portal verbatim: 'Click the link for your free return label: https://automic.aftership.com. AfterShip is available for U.S residents only.' Dead URL response: page title '404 Not Found - Automic Gold'.
findings.action: policy_source repointed to the live refund-policy page; resize_policy blanked with a note so the owning session can restore it with a verbatim quote. Recorded as flag SRC1.
findings.subject: S-AUTOMIC

findings.title: Sarraf counts returns over $10,000 as 'high-risk' behaviour under a three-strike policy
findings.detail: Sarraf's live returns policy publishes a 'NOTICE OF EXCESSIVE RETURNS' defining high-risk return behaviour as 'Returning 30 or more items', 'Returning purchases greater than $10K' or an 'Overall return rate of 85%'. Clients who reach three strikes 'will be prohibited from making any new orders'. Strikes are not assessed where the fault is Sarraf's, for example a damaged or incorrectly listed item. A buyer returning an expensive engagement ring can therefore be counted as high-risk purely because of the item's price. This is a seller-reputation and return-friendliness fact that the checklist's 'return policy' item should carry, and it is now recorded as flag RET13 and on the S-SARRAF record.
findings.evidence: Verbatim: 'The Sarraf.com operates on a three strike policy for clients who exhibit high-risk return behavior. High-risk behavior is identified as: Returning 30 or more items; Returning purchases greater than $10K; Overall return rate of 85%.' and 'Clients who reach three strikes will be prohibited from making any new orders.'
findings.action: Published as flag RET13 on the Sarraf record and on the flagged-for-review page. Treat the return right as usable but consequential: return decisively, once.
findings.subject: S-SARRAF

findings.title: Two official Sarraf pages contradict each other on whether engraved rings can be returned
findings.detail: Sarraf's About page describes the 30-day policy as covering 'any non-engraved items still in new condition and we'll give you a full refund within the first 30 days. No questions asked.' The returns policy page says the opposite for engraved rings: 'Any ring where personal engraving was added or a special finish may be returned, exchanged, or resized where possible (with the exception of special orders); however, the $25.00 engraving fee or $50.00 finsh charges are non-refundable.' One page excludes engraved items outright, the other accepts them with non-refundable fees. data/sellers.json had previously recorded the stricter reading as a flat exclusion ('Custom-sized, special-order, or engraved items do not qualify'), which is not what either page says on its own. Where two official pages conflict, a buyer should assume the stricter one applies until the seller confirms otherwise in writing.
findings.evidence: About page verbatim: '30-Day Return Policy - Return any non-engraved items still in new condition and we'll give you a full refund within the first 30 days. No questions asked.' Returns page verbatim: 'CAN I RETURN OR RESIZE AN ENGRAVED RING? Any ring where personal engraving was added or a special finish may be returned, exchanged, or resized where possible (with the exception of special orders); however, the $25.00 engraving fee or $50.00 finsh charges are non-refundable.'
findings.action: Recorded as flag SPEC4 with both URLs; S-SARRAF resize_policy corrected to quote both pages. Do not engrave until the return window has passed, or get written confirmation first.
findings.subject: S-SARRAF

findings.title: Three Catbird values drafted in this pass did not survive contact with the live pages
findings.detail: The same defect class this pass hunts in other sessions appeared in its own draft data. An intermediate version of the S-CB record carried hello@catbirdnyc.com as Catbird's e-mail, '219 Bedford Avenue, Brooklyn, NY 11211' as a return address, and a final-sale list reading 'pierced earrings, body jewelry, items from the Final Sale collection, gift cards'. Re-fetching both pages on 2026-10-23 showed: the contact page publishes customerservice@catbirdnyc.com for order, availability, product and shipping questions (plus two role-specific addresses that are not customer service); the returns page publishes no postal return address at all, only a Narvar return portal and in-store returns; and the actual final-sale list is 'Special orders, engraved items, Forever jewelry, earrings from piercing events, home & beauty items, and comestibles' - the earlier wording had been carried over from data/retailers.json rather than from Catbird's own page. All three were corrected or blanked. The page also adds two facts a buyer needs: 'Once your order is placed we are unable to cancel it or make changes', and there is no exchange - 'place a new order on line for your new size. This is currently the only way we are able to accomodate exchanges.'
findings.evidence: Contact page verbatim: 'Order Status, Availability, Product Details or Shipping Questions - customerservice@catbirdnyc.com'. Returns page verbatim: 'Special orders, engraved items, Forever jewelry, earrings from piercing events, home & beauty items, and comestibles are final sale and cannot be returned.' and 'An $9 charge for return shipping will be deducted from your refund.' and 'All international sales are final.'
findings.action: Corrected in data/sellers.json: email set to customerservice@catbirdnyc.com, return_address set to null with a note, exclusions replaced with the page's own list, and the no-cancellation and return-then-reorder rules added as their own fields.
findings.subject: S-CB

findings.title: Catbird's /contact-us page returned HTTP 500 on 2026-10-23 live re-verification
findings.detail: During live re-verification on 2026-10-23, Catbird's /contact-us URL returned an nginx 500 Internal Server Error, whereas Catbird's official /facts and /returns pages returned HTTP 200 and confirm customerservice@catbirdnyc.com verbatim.

findings.evidence: catbirdnyc.com/contact-us returned nginx '500 Internal Server Error' on 2026-10-23; catbirdnyc.com/facts returned HTTP 200: 'Customer Email: customerservice@catbirdnyc.com'.

findings.title: All 7 Aurate lab-grown engagement ring PDPs enforce 'Exchange for size only. Final Sale!' beside 'Free Returns' and omit listing-level 'solid' wording
findings.detail: Opening all seven exact Aurate PDPs live on 2026-10-23 (AU5760 $2,858, AU5769 $2,638, AU5000 $1,498, AU5093 $1,968, AU5763 $2,858, AU5764 $3,958, AU5107 $2,498) confirmed every page prints 'Exchange for size only. Final Sale!' directly beside a 'Free Returns' badge, prints only 'Rate - 14k GOLD' (no 'solid' on the PDP itself), shares multi-variant weights ('5.5-8.5g', '5.7-8.7g', '5.9-8.9g', '2.23g', '2.36g', '3.33g') inclusive of stone carats, and misstates 'classic oval diamond' on Emerald Bezel SKU AU5093.

findings.detail: Line-by-line inspection of live PDPs on 2026-10-23 uncovered copy-paste specification bugs in structured product tables: Brilliant Earth sid=39897151 prints 'Band Width: 2 ct. tw.' (carat units in millimeter field) and geo-routes non-US readers to EUR pricing, while VRAI Petite 4-Prong Solitaire prints 'Pavé carat weight: 0.11ctw' when the Plain (stone-free) band is selected.

findings.title: Ring Concierge's $6,038 engagement-ring page claims both a 2.08 ct E VS1 stone and a 5.63 ct D VVS2 stone — and cuts the return window to 7 days
findings.detail: Live re-read of Ring Concierge's 2.08 Oval Lab Diamond in Whisper Thin Hidden Halo on 2026-10-23 uncovered two major contradictions: (1) the title and Details accordion specify '2.08 Carat E VS1 Oval Lab Grown Diamond', while the description prose directly on the same page claims 'featuring a 5.63 Carat D VVS2 Oval Lab Diamond'; and (2) while Ring Concierge's general Refund Policy states 30 days on Fine Jewelry, the engagement-ring PDP Shipping & Returns accordion states 'You have 1 week (7 days) from the date of delivery to return your ready-made engagement ring' and makes any resized ring final sale.
findings.evidence: Title/Details: '2.08 Carat E VS1 Oval Lab Grown Diamond' vs Description: 'featuring a 5.63 Carat D VVS2 Oval Lab Diamond' · PDP FAQ: '1 week (7 days) from the date of delivery to return your ready-made engagement ring'
findings.action: Require the exact diamond certificate number and written return window before ordering, and assume the stricter 7-day bridal return window governs.

findings.title: Systematic URL sweep caught five more 404 citations, two mis-transcribed phone numbers, and Menē's JS-gated weights

findings.title: Live gold spot fell 0.62% on the same market date, and the page's own clock label runs backwards
findings.detail: The GoldPrice.org page was opened again on 2026-10-23 at 20:17Z and printed “Spot Gold Price: USD 3,997.22 / Ounce … Oct 23rd, 2026 at 04:17 NY Time”, with the header ticker reading “3,996.89 / -47.83 / -1.18%”. The stored primary snapshot in data/prices.json is USD 4,022.22 / oz labelled “Oct 23rd, 2026 at 05:55 NY Time”. Two things follow. First, the stored snapshot is now 0.62% above the live reading; because it is a dated capture, it was deliberately NOT overwritten — every melt and break-even figure on this site is arithmetic on that documented number, and silently replacing it would change every printed result. Second, the live page's clock label (04:17 NY) is EARLIER than the label on the morning's capture (05:55 NY) even though it was read some ten hours later, so at least one of the two timestamps is not what it appears to be. This project records that instead of inventing an explanation for it.
findings.evidence: Live 2026-10-23T20:17Z: “Spot Gold Price: USD 3,997.22 / Ounce | Spot Silver Price: USD 53.92 / Ounce Oct 23rd, 2026 at 04:17 NY Time” (https://goldprice.org/). Stored: USD 4,022.22 at “Oct 23rd, 2026 at 05:55 NY Time” (data/prices.json, snapshot goldprice-org-2026-10-23). Difference: $25.00/oz = 0.6215%.
findings.impact: Melt values move by the same 0.62%. Working the arithmetic with the project's exact constants (1 troy ounce = 31.1034768 g, 14K fineness 14/24): gold is $129.3174/g pure and $75.4351/g at 14K on the stored $4,022.22/oz, and $128.5136/g pure and $74.9663/g at 14K on the live $3,997.22/oz. R20's 3.80 g 14K ring therefore holds $286.65 of gold at the stored spot and $284.87 at the live one — $1.78 less, the same 0.62%. Every 'price ÷ melt' multiple printed on the site shifts by that amount.
findings.action: Re-read the spot source on the day you use the calculator; treat every figure on this site as dated. The timestamp inversion is published for review rather than resolved by assumption.
findings.source_note: Live reading taken 2026-10-23T20:17Z; the stored snapshot it is compared against is in data/prices.json.

findings.title: The live spot reading is corroborated by four feeds to 0.026% — and is published, not used
findings.detail: Pass P14 read four independent publishers at 2026-10-23T20:17Z: GoldPrice.org $3,997.22/oz, Kitco bid $3,996.20/oz, BullionVault $3,997.14/oz and the World Gold Council tile $3,996.31/oz. It is deliberately NOT promoted to the calculation anchor: two earlier sessions kept the dated snapshot so every melt figure stays reproducible (F39), and the stored numbers were left untouched. If a current-price melt figure is wanted, `scripts/refresh_spot_anchor.py` performs the re-anchor reproducibly from one dated capture and keeps the superseded snapshot as history.

findings.action: Read the melt column as dated. To move the anchor, run scripts/refresh_spot_anchor.py against a fresh capture rather than editing JSON by hand.

findings.title: A prior verification record credits a NIST page with a conversion figure it does not print
findings.detail: data/reverification-c-6ccbc523.json says NIST Precious Metals Conversion Information 'explicitly confirms 1 oz t = 31.1034768 g'. Pass P15 re-read that URL on 2026-10-23: it returns HTTP 200 and reproduces NIST Handbook 130 sec. 2.17 with a linked conversion PDF, but prints no troy-ounce-to-gram figure. The numeric constant is nevertheless valid: NIST SP 811 Appendix B.9 prints troy ounce = 3.110 348 E+01 g and the boldface/exact grain factor 6.479 891 E-05 kg; exactly 480 grains per troy ounce gives 31.1034768 g.
findings.evidence: NIST SP 811 B.9: 'ounce (troy or apothecary) (oz) -> gram (g) | 3.110 348 | E+01'; 'grain (gr) -> kilogram (kg) | 6.479 891 | E-05' (boldface = exact). 480 x 0.06479891 = 31.1034768.
findings.action: No melt figure changes: the constant is correct. The citation and derivation are now explicit in spot-and-standards.json. The peer historical evidence file was not overwritten; CR-P15-1 records the documentation request.
